title: Interactions: Fix state reset bug when switching stories with date mocks
body:
Closes #32834 

## What I did

Forced a reset of `lastRenderId` when switching stories, to ensure we account for the fact that `Date.now()` can be mocked in a story.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### Manual testing

1. Build a canary for this PR
2. Install it on https://github.com/Sidnioulz/storybook-play-function-error-state-persistence-repro
3. Launch Storybook
4. Go to http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/example-frog--late which triggers a caught exception state
5. Navigate to http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/example-frog--on-time-too and see the state is cleared

Without the canary, the state will not be properly cleared.

**Fix TypeScript type error on line 252.**

The logic in lines 276-283 correctly handles story switches with mocked `Date.now()`. However, line 252 has a type annotation error: `useRef<string>(undefined)` is invalid under strict TypeScript mode since `undefined` is not assignable to `string`.

Change to:
```typescript
const lastStoryId = useRef<string | undefined>(undefined);
```

This matches the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., `TourGuide.tsx`).

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/core/src/component-testing/components/Panel.tsx around lines 252 and
276-283, the ref declaration uses useRef<string>(undefined) which fails under
strict TypeScript because undefined isn't assignable to string; change the type
to allow undefined (e.g., useRef<string | undefined>(undefined)) so lastStoryId
can be initialized with undefined and match the usage in the render-id logic
where it's compared against event.storyId.
```

</details>

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
Good point. I've also added a comment to explain why we care about lastRenderId, and renamed it latestRenderId to
* make it easier to distinguish from lastStoryId
* clarify that we pick the latest render when it comes into effect

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Just wondering whether this should always be `0` rather than `event.renderId`, or would that break things? Not sure.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: If we don't initialise it to the id for the current event, then we'll hit the code below that bails out when multiple concurrent renders exist.
